newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia 10-yr plan aims to develop key industries.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia 10-yr plan aims to develop key industries.

text.p: Malaysia unveiled a 10-year master plan for industry on Thursday which it said will focus on developing eight key sectors up to the year 2005.
The Second Industrial Master Plan, launched by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, picks up from where the first plan, effective between 1986-1995, ended.

Under the previous plan, which focused on large investments and rapid industrialisation, Malaysia attracted substantial foreign capital and technology to maintain economic growth of over eight percent for the past nine years.

The eight key areas of industry identified for further development were electrical and electronics, textiles and appparel, chemicals, resource-based industries, agro-based and food products industries, transport, materials, and machinery.

Under the new plan, the manufacturing sector is projected to grow 10.7 percent a year until the year 2000 and slow to an average of 8.3 percent a year until 2005, said the Ministry of International Trade and Industry, which prepared the plan.
"This relatively lower growth of the manufacturing sector is in line with the optimum growth pattern experienced in most developed economies," the ministry said.
Economists said the plan was focused on finding ways to reduce import dependence.
The ministry said the plan will be implemented on a "rolling basis", meaning it will be monitored and reviewed periodically to accomodate changes in the global economy.

Strategies include improving the country's economic foundation, developing manufacturing sub-sectors, speeding up development of indigenous technology and marketing capabilities and reducing high imports of intermediate and capital goods.

Economists said the development of local support industries was a logical step for Malaysia, which has transformed itself from an agricultural to an export-driven industrial economy in just over a decade. It aims to become a fully industrialised nation by 2020.
The cluster-based industrial development approach under the plan should provide for a "broad-based, resilient and internationally competitive industrial sector", the ministry said.

The manufacturing sector is expected to account for 37.5 percent and 38.4 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2000 and 2005, respectively. Last year, manufacturing contributed 33.1 percent of GDP.
The sector is projected to need total investments of 250 billion ringgit ($100 billion) or 25 billion ringgit annually during the next 10 years.
Manufacturing exports are expected to grow 16 percent a year during the next decade.

The share of manufacturing employment to total employment is expected to grow from 26.2 percent in 1996 to 29.4 percent in 2005, with an estimated 2.8 million workers in the sector towards the end of the plan.
